title: Contes extraordinaires
summary: "Contes extraordinaires" by Ernest Hello is a collection of short stories written in the late 19th century. Blending parable, mysticism, and Catholic moral reflection, the tales probe the search for the Name of God, the dignity of the poor, and the treachery of appearances. Early pieces focus on figures like Ludovic, an avaricious patriarch, and William, a renowned doctor consumed by an unnamed hunger, to explore conscience, charity, and spiritual blindness. The opening of the collection presents a preface that champions the conte as a humble, piercing vehicle for truth, framing the book between the Name of God and the name of the poor, and exalting charity’s mysterious power. The first tale, Ludovic, follows a wealthy family’s collapse as the father’s fanatic avarice strips away comfort and love; he hoards gold in a secret cellar, locks it with a code word—then forgets it—and, while trying to sell the household’s last friend, the dog Mirro, is killed as he recognizes the lost word too late. The next story begins with Dr. William, a famous physician wasting away because no food matches a vague, absolute craving; in private notes he recalls meeting a mysterious presence who called him “my child” and seemed to promise a higher science, hinting at the spiritual enigma driving his decline.
